「排場」與「出陣」是兩種不同的演奏狀態。: Paichang, playing seated at a fixed spot, and chuzhen, playing on the move with the procession, are two different states of playing.
不同曲館之間有聯誼、有競賽、也有因為曲目與風格不同而形成的派別。西皮與福祿的區分: Different quguan have friendly ties with each other and competitions, and also schools that form around differences of repertoire and style. The split between Xipi and Fulu rests partly on these distinctions between quguan: the quguan of one area may lean towards one system, and the zidi learn that one inside it.
主奏牌子；戲曲段落中跟腔伴奏並加花裝飾，音量最大，是戶外的主導聲部: Carries the pai tunes; in opera sections it follows the vocal line and adds ornament, and it is the loudest voice, the leading part outdoors
先聽鼓。鼓點是段落的標記，聽到鼓換了打法，就知道段落變了。: Listen to the drum first. The drum patterns are the markers of sections; when the drum changes its pattern you know the section has changed.
兩者是不同的系統，音高、風格、曲目與演奏習慣都有差別。在台灣，不同地區的曲館可能: They are two different systems, differing in pitch, style, repertoire and playing habits. In Taiwan the quguan of different areas may lean towards one system or the other, competing and exchanging as they go.
兩者是台灣漢人音樂的兩個不同傳統。南管以琵琶、洞簫、三弦、二弦為核心，風格細緻、: They are two different traditions of Han Taiwanese music. Nanguan is built around the pipa, dongxiao, sanxian and erxian, fine in style and slow in tempo; beiguan is built on the suona and on gongs and drums, loud and forceful. The instruments, the repertoire and the social function all differ.
再聽嗩吶。它是外場的主旋律，音量大、裝飾多；注意它在句尾的收法，那往往是段落的接: Then listen to the suona. It carries the main melody outdoors, loud and heavily ornamented; notice how it closes a phrase, which is often where the next section joins.
分辨鑼鼓層與旋律層。北管的鑼鼓不只是伴奏，它有自己的段落；試著在不聽旋律的情況下: Tell the gong-and-drum layer apart from the melody layer. In beiguan the gongs and drums are not just accompaniment; they have sections of their own. Try listening to them alone, without following the melody.
北管和南管是同一種音樂，只是地區不同。: Beiguan and nanguan are the same music, only from different regions.
北管是台灣漢人聚落裡的業餘合奏傳統，以嗩吶與鑼鼓為骨幹，加上弦樂與笛，分西皮與福: Beiguan is the amateur ensemble tradition of Han Taiwanese settlements, built on suona and gongs and drums with strings and flute added, and divided into the Xipi and Fulu systems. It is not an art played in concert halls: it is played by local zidi, in quguan and xuanshe (amateur clubs of young men), at temple fairs, processions, weddings, funerals and celebrations. What keeps it alive is not professional musicians but amateur members of a community, passed down from one generation to the next.
北管是職業樂師的音樂，由專業團體演出。: Beiguan is the music of professional musicians, performed by professional groups.
北管的場合是廟會、神明遶境、建醮、婚禮、喪禮、開幕與地方慶典。它與寺廟的關係最深: Beiguan is played at temple fairs, processions of the gods, jiao offering festivals, weddings, funerals, openings and local celebrations. Its tie to the temple is the deepest: at a temple fair the quguan goes out and plays paichang in front of the temple, performing pai tunes and gong-and-drum pieces; on a procession it walks in the line, clearing the way with suona and drums. Weddings and funerals use beiguan too, but with different repertoire and tempo — funerals use slow, restrained sections.
北管的核心是業餘的子弟曲館：成員有自己的職業，練習與出陣是社區事務。這種業餘性不: At the centre of beiguan are the amateur zidi quguan: the members have their own jobs, and practice and going out are community affairs. This amateur status is not a defect; it is the social structure the tradition survives on.
北管的編制分兩大塊：吹打與弦樂。吹打是外場，聲音大、投射遠，用於行進與戶外；弦樂: The beiguan line-up falls into two blocks: wind-and-percussion and strings. Wind and percussion are the outer field, loud and far-carrying, used for marching and outdoors; the strings are the inner field, quieter, used indoors or to accompany singing. A quguan usually has both and deploys them according to the occasion. The instruments are not arranged like symphonic sections but by how loud they actually are relative to each other.
北管的聲音分兩層：鑼鼓層與旋律層。鑼鼓層不只是一組拍點，它有自己的段落結構——同: The beiguan sound has two layers: gongs and drums, and melody. The gong-and-drum layer is not just a set of beats; it has a sectional structure of its own — the same gong-and-drum pattern can go on for a long time with the melody running above it or between it. Because the gongs and drums are themselves a section, beiguan can be played on percussion alone, for marching, openings and transitions.
協調方式靠鼓與領奏。北管沒有指揮，鼓手用鼓點帶段落，嗩吶手用旋律帶句子，其他樂手: Coordination comes from the drum and the lead players. Beiguan has no conductor: the drummer carries the sections with drum patterns, the suona player carries the phrases with melody, and everyone else listens to those two. On the march the line stretches out and the back cannot hear the front, so it relies on the sheer volume of drum and suona cutting through the crowd. Indoors the volume drops, coordination becomes finer, and it relies on eye contact and breathing.
台灣北管（Beiguan）— 台灣漢人聚落中以嗩吶、鑼鼓與弦樂組成的業餘合奏傳統: Beiguan — an amateur ensemble tradition of Han Taiwanese settlements, built on suona, gongs and drums and strings, in two systems, Xipi and Fulu. Ensembles and instrumentation by Next Door Sound Weavers.
和中國鑼鼓相比，差別在有沒有旋律聲部。鑼鼓是純打擊編制，以單一領奏鼓（戲曲中多為: Compared with Chinese luogu, the difference is whether there is a melodic part at all. Luogu is a purely percussive line-up, led by a single leading drum (usually the ban drum in opera) with gongs and cymbals answering, and remembered through the spoken luogu jing. In beiguan the gongs and drums are only one layer, with suona, flute and strings above them, and the three repertoire types — pai, xianpu and opera — each match a different line-up and occasion.
和南管相比，差別在音量、樂器與社會功能。南管以琵琶、洞簫、三弦、二弦為核心，音量: Compared with nanguan, the difference is volume, instruments and social function. Nanguan is built around the pipa, dongxiao, sanxian and erxian, quiet and slow, suited to quiet indoor listening; beiguan is built on suona and gongs and drums, voiced for temple fairs, processions and marching, and a single quguan even has two playing states, paichang and chuzhen.
和國樂團相比，差別在業餘性與編制規模。國樂團有指揮、有總譜、樂器被擴充成高音到低: Compared with a Chinese orchestra, the difference is amateur status and scale. A Chinese orchestra has a conductor and a full score, and its instruments are expanded into a family from high to low; beiguan is an amateur organisation of zidi in a community quguan, its line-up deployed according to the occasion, its repertoire carried by oral transmission and manuscript books, and its players start on gongs and drums or simple strings.
大廣弦奏音域較低的旋律線；北管弦樂以齊奏與異音織體為主，並非西方意義的低音與和聲: The daguangxian plays a melody line in a lower range; beiguan strings work mainly in unison and in heterophonic texture, not in the Western division into bass and harmony
弦譜是絲竹曲，以弦樂與笛為主，不用嗩吶，音量小，用於室內。它的旋律比較細緻，段落: Xianpu are silk-and-bamboo pieces for strings and flute, without suona, quiet, played indoors. Their melodies are more finely worked, the joins between sections are fixed, and they are often what a quguan plays when it meets.
弦譜與室內段落的主奏，音色較細: Leads the xianpu and the indoor sections, with a finer timbre
後場與前場的關係也值得注意。戲曲段落裡，演唱者（前場）決定句子的長短與裝飾，樂隊: The relation between the back stage and the front stage is worth noting too. In opera sections the singer on the front stage decides the length of phrases and the ornament, and the band on the back stage follows his breathing and diction; change the singer for the same passage and the drummer's cues and the suona's joins all have to change. This relation, in which the band serves the vocal line, is the exact reverse of the pai tunes, where the suona leads and the gongs and drums follow it, and it is why a beiguan player needs two kinds of ear at once.
戲曲段落由人聲擔任主旋律，樂隊跟著唱腔走: In opera sections the human voice carries the melody and the band follows the vocal line
戲曲（亂彈）是有唱腔的段落，樂隊跟著演唱者走。唱腔的段落由鼓手提示，嗩吶或弦樂跟: Opera (luantan) is the section with singing, where the band follows the singer. The drummer cues the sung sections, and the suona or strings follow the melody and breathing of the vocal line; the same passage, sung by a different singer, takes different ornament and tempo, and the band has to adjust.
打出重音、製造張力，與鼓共同構成鑼鼓層: Marks the accents and builds tension, forming the gong-and-drum layer together with the drum
找室內的弦譜錄音。音量小、音色細，和戶外牌子的聲響完全是兩回事。: Look for an indoor xianpu recording. Quiet, finely timbred — a completely different sound from the outdoor pai tunes.
指揮整團：起板、轉段、收尾都由鼓帶: Directs the whole group: the opening, the change of section and the close are all carried by the drum
排場是在廟前或廣場定點坐著演奏，可以完整走完一套牌子或一段戲曲；出陣是隨著遶境隊: Paichang is playing seated at a fixed spot in front of a temple or in a square, where a whole set of pai tunes or a whole opera section can be played through. Chuzhen is playing on the move with the procession, where only sections are taken, short phrases repeated, and the point is for the sound to be there continuously. The same repertoire has a beginning, development and close in paichang; in chuzhen it is cut into fragments that can be broken off and picked up again at any moment. Players must be able to do both, because one temple fair often needs both.
曲目分三類：牌子（吹打）、弦譜（絲竹）、戲曲（亂彈唱腔）。三類對應不同的場合與編: The repertoire falls into three types: pai (wind and percussion), xianpu (silk and bamboo) and opera (luantan song). Each matches a different occasion and line-up: pai for outdoors and paichang, xianpu for indoor gatherings, opera for occasions with singing.
曲館的成員有自己的職業，練習在晚上或農閒，演奏的曲目靠口傳與抄本，代代傳承。這種: Members of a quguan have their own jobs, practise in the evening or in the slack farming season, and learn the repertoire through oral transmission and manuscript books, generation after generation. This way of passing things on leaves small differences between quguan: the same qupai may be ornamented and paced differently in two of them. Such differences are not mistakes but the actual state of the tradition.
曲館的組織也決定了樂隊怎麼運作。一個曲館通常有負責人、有固定的練習場所（常是廟宇: How a quguan is organised also decides how the band works. A quguan usually has a person in charge, a fixed place to practise (often a side room of a temple or a community centre), instruments and manuscripts held in common, and a contact who arranges engagements to go out. Members stand in teacher-and-student relations and also learn from their peers; newcomers start on gongs and drums or simple strings and only take up the suona or a lead part once they are familiar. The line-up for going out is arranged according to the occasion and the number of people available: a big temple fair has many, a small wedding or funeral may send only a few.
業餘性本身影響了聲音。: Amateur status itself shapes the sound.
注意西皮與福祿的差別。同一個曲牌，兩個系統的音高與氣質不同；聽久了會分辨得出來。: Listen for the difference between Xipi and Fulu. The same qupai has a different pitch and temperament in the two systems; after a while you can tell them apart.
演唱者（票友或子弟）: Singer (a piaoyou amateur or a zidi)
牌子、弦譜、戲曲是三種不同的曲目類型，運作方式也不同。: Pai tunes, xianpu and opera are three different repertoire types, and they work differently.
牌子是吹打曲，以嗩吶為主，鑼鼓伴奏，結構固定、氣勢大，用於排場、遶境與慶典的開場: Pai are wind-and-percussion pieces, led by the suona with gongs and drums accompanying, fixed in structure and forceful, used to open paichang, processions and celebrations. Their sections are marked by drum patterns and the suona follows a fixed melody; what players remember is this section after that one, not a piece from beginning to end.
西皮的旋律比較高、比較亮，福祿比較低、比較沉。兩個系統各有自己的曲目與演奏習慣；: Xipi melodies sit higher and sound brighter; Fulu sits lower and heavier. Each system has its own repertoire and playing habits, and in Taiwan the quguan of different areas may lean towards one of them, competing and exchanging as they do. Xipi is also called the new road and Fulu the old road; this new/old division reflects the order in which the two repertoires and vocal styles arrived locally and settled, not a difference of instruments. When the same set of instruments plays the repertoire of a different system, the pitch, the ornament and the habits of phrasing are all different.
西皮與福祿只是名稱不同，曲目與演奏方式一樣。: Xipi and Fulu are just different names; the repertoire and the way of playing are the same.
西皮與福祿是兩個系統，差別在音高與風格。: Xipi and Fulu are two systems, differing in pitch and style.
這個編制的核心是「鼓指揮、嗩吶帶旋律」。鼓手不是打拍子的節拍器，而是整團的指揮：: At the heart of this line-up is the principle that the drum directs and the suona carries the melody. The drummer is not a metronome keeping time but the group's conductor: by different drum patterns he tells the players when to start, when to turn and when to close. The suona player leads the melody: in the pai tunes the suona plays its melody inside the fixed gong-and-drum patterns (gujie) while the drum patterns mark the changes of section; in xianpu the strings and flute form sections of their own; in opera the strings follow the singer.
這種「曲館對曲館」的關係，是北管在台灣的實際生態。: This quguan-to-quguan relation is what beiguan actually looks like in Taiwan.
音量與場合的關係也很直接。牌子的嗩吶與鑼鼓是為戶外與行進設計的，聲音大、投射遠；: The relation between volume and occasion is direct too. The suona and gongs of the pai tunes are voiced for outdoors and marching, loud and far-carrying; xianpu are voiced for indoors, quiet and finely timbred. That one quguan can manage both occasions comes from the same people changing instruments and repertoire, not from hiring a different band. This flexibility — one set of people, two kinds of sound — is how an amateur quguan meets many occasions with limited manpower.
